findings.claim: The architecture overview's row for kmctl plugin patch still says "--undo deletes the plugin folder and the OpenCode files" with no scope, which is now false at --scope user.

The r3 test checks the reference only for "With `--scope user`" and the word "leaves", which appears many times elsewhere in commands.md, so it would still pass if the new sentence stopped saying the files are left and named.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks for.
At `--scope user`, `unpatch` returns before any delete and builds one note from the Antigravity folder and `opencode.undo_paths`.
Project scope runs the same path as before, and `undo` now deletes what `undo_paths` names.
The gates are green.
Two small non-blocking findings remain: a stale line in the architecture overview and a weak docs test.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r4 all pass.
It printed `stamp green: 42215e19883ecd61d3f0ea7526292123654cfa6d75a376534b338738ed90f2dd`.
I ran the plan's measurement script on the worktree.
It printed `exit 0 deleted 0 changed 0`.
I read the `undo` refactor in `src/kmctl/opencode.py` line by line.
`undo_paths` adds opencode.json only when `instructions` is a list that holds `INSTRUCTIONS`, so the `_instructions` call in `undo` cannot raise.
An unreadable opencode.json is still skipped while the agents, rules and plugin still go, as before.
Folder cleanup is unchanged.
In `src/kmctl/plugin.py`, the user-scope branch deletes nothing and adds a note only when something is found.
The CLI still prints `nothing to undo` when there are no notes, and `Next: kmctl doctor --scope user` after that.
r1: both `undo_user_scope` tests compare the full file tree before and after.
They check exit 0 through `_patch`, every OpenCode path or the plugin folder in the note, and the `kmctl plugin patch --undo` and `without --scope user` text.
r2: the existing project-scope undo tests (`test_undo_leaves_no_kmctl_file`, `test_undo_deletes_only_the_plugin_folder` and others) still run under `-k undo`.
The new `test_undo_user_scope_with_nothing_here_says_nothing_to_undo` checks for no `note:` and exit 0.
`test_undo_paths_name_what_undo_removes` checks that the two functions agree.
r3: I read the new help, epilog and reference text myself (judgment).
They say that user scope leaves the repository's files and names them.
The test is weak (f2).
Consistency: README, the two how-to pages and ADR 0024 describe project-scope removal and stay true.
The overview row does not (f1).
f1: `.okf/architecture/overview.md` line 180 ends with "`--undo` deletes the plugin folder and the OpenCode files".
Add "at project scope", or say that user scope names them and leaves them.

f2: `test_undo_docs_say_user_scope_leaves_project_files` should check a phrase that only the new sentence holds, for example "deletes nothing in this repository" in the reference and "names them" in the help.
The new sentence in `docs/reference/commands.md` line 488 is joined to the previous line without a rewrap.
That is cosmetic.
